source.section: Instructions PDF pp.9-10, Schedule M line 1t, questions 1 and 2 and table lines 1-4; Worksheet Step 1 lines 1-7, Step 2 lines 8-13 and instructions PDF p.9, Schedule M line 1s; Instructions PDF p.4, RI-1040 lines 1-5; PDF p.5, lines 6-8; PDF p.13, Tax Computation Worksheet ('Use for all filing status types')

worked: Federal AGI = private pension (person 0) 60,000.00 + private pension (person 1) 10,050.00 + taxable Social Security 34,000.00 + interest 29,700.00 = 133,750.00. Federal taxable income = 133,750.00 - 31,500.00 standard deduction - 2 x 1,600.00 age 65+ = 99,050.00 (given, not tested; federal senior deduction ignored). RI-1040 line 1 federal AGI 133,750.00. Line 1s, Social Security worksheet: person 0 born 1950-06-15 (age 75), person 1 born 1951-06-15 (age 74). Line 3 federal AGI 133,750.00; line 4 Married filing jointly; line 5 born on or before 03/01/1959: yes; line 6 133,750.00; line 7 133,750.00 less than 133,750.00: no. STOP: not eligible; modification 0.00. Line 1t: question 1 born on or before March 1, 1959: person 0 born 1950-06-15 (age 75), person 1 born 1951-06-15 (age 74): yes; question 2 federal AGI 133,750.00 less than or equal to 133,750.00: yes. Table: person 0 line 2 60,000.00, line 3 lesser of that and 50,000.00 = 50,000.00; person 1 line 2 10,050.00, line 3 lesser of that and 50,000.00 = 10,050.00; line 4 = 60,050.00. Line 1y total decreasing modifications = 60,050.00. Line 2a other-state obligations 0.00; line 2m total increasing modifications = 0.00. Schedule M page 2 line 3 net = 0.00 - 60,050.00 = -60,050.00; RI-1040 line 2 = -60,050.00. Line 3 modified federal AGI = 133,750.00 + (-60,050.00) = 73,700.00. Standard Deduction and Exemption Worksheets: line 3 73,700.00 is not more than 254,250.00: the worksheets stop at line 3, full amounts. Line 4 standard deduction: 21,800.00 (Married filing jointly). Line 5 = 73,700.00 - 21,800.00 = 51,900.00. Line 6 exemptions: 2 x 5,100.00 = 10,200.00. Line 7 taxable income = 51,900.00 - 10,200.00 = 41,700.00. Line 8 tax on 41,700.00 by the schedule as numbers: 41,700.00 x 0.0375 = 1563.750000 = 1,563.75. Credits 0.00 (Schedule I, Schedule II, RI earned income credit and RI-1040H are not modelled and not claimed here). Rhode Island income tax = 1,563.75. Note: Federal AGI exactly 133,750: the two tests split here. Line 1t question 2 is 'less than or equal to', so the pension stays; worksheet line 7 is 'less than', so Social Security is lost.
accepted_approximations: The pension test keeps the relief at exactly the limit, as instructions line 1t asks ('less than or equal to'); the statute printed in the Guide says 'less than'.
